The probability of failure is extremely sensitive to the distribution function of the efﬂuent concentration. After this distribution is known, an expression may be found to deﬁne the fraction of time that a given concentration has been exceeded in the past and, consequently, the future perfor- mance of the plant can be predicted, provided process variables and conditions remain the same.

Because of variations in performance, a WWTP should be designed to produce an average efﬂuent concentration below the discharge standards. A mean value should be used to guarantee an efﬂuent concentration consistently less than a standard with a certain reliability level. [Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [(1979)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) developed a coefﬁcient of reliability (COR) that relates mean constituent values (i.e. design or operational value) to the standards that must be achieved on a probability basis. This methodology has been used and recommended in two important textbooks ([Crites](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Tchobanoglous,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2000;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Metcalf](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Eddy,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2003)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) and used or consulted by several authors in the last 25 years ([Quek](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1995;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Naval](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Wanderley,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2000;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Etnier](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2005;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Gupta](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Shrivastava,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2006)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese).

The concepts associated with coefﬁcient of variation (CV) and COR can be used in the following ways. Firstly, for an existing legislation, a treatment plant should be designed in order to accommodate the expected future variability of its efﬂuent (based on CV values from similar existing plants) such that the discharge standard will hopefully be satisﬁed within the required percentage. Secondly, for an existing treatment plant, operational practices should be such that the resulting efﬂuent, with its mean concentration and variability (CV value), could lead to the required percentage of com- pliance with the standard. Finally, from the regulator’s point of view, if real CV values from treatment plants and different processes are known, sensible and affordable discharge standards can be speciﬁed.

This method has been used, in this study, for the determination of the COR for efﬂuent concentrations for different CVs related to six treatment technologies (166 full- scale urban WWTP). The design concentrations necessary to meet the prevailing BOD, COD, TSS, TN, TP and FC discharge standards and the expected compliance percentages have been calculated from the COR values achieved. The following treatment processes have been analyzed: (a) septic tank followed by anaerobic ﬁlter (ST+AF), (b) facultative ponds (FP), (c) anaerobic ponds followed by FPs (AP+FP), (d) activated sludge (AS), (e) upﬂow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactors and (f) UASB reactors followed by several post- treatment types (UASB+POST).

The importance of the study is ampliﬁed by the fact that there is a lack of similar research covering the above- mentioned treatment technologies. The original works by [Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [(1979)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) concentrated on the AS process and [Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [(1982)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) on trickling ﬁlters. In the literature surveyed, no study was found that has made a comparison of the expected reliability among different treatment technologies. A large number of data has been analyzed in this research, amplify- ing its importance for developing countries, for which the existing knowledge of the performance of WWTPs in opera- tion is relatively sparse, with little structured consolidations in terms of overall evaluations.

## 2. Methods

2.1. Coefﬁcient of reliability (COR)

A series of studies published about the distribution of the concentration data from WWTP (most of them considering BOD and TSS) report that the lognormal distribution gives a good overall ﬁt to efﬂuent concentration values ([Dean](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Forsythe,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1976a,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [b;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Schroeder,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1981;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1979,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1981,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1982;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Berthouex](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [and](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Hunter,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1981,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1983;](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [Charles](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2005)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese). In order to conﬁrm this assumption, an extensive characterization of the distributions of the constituents was undertaken, based on data from 35 WWTPs operating in Brazil ([Oliveira,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [2006)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese). The study aimed at determining the best theoretical probability distribution to describe the behavior of the variables biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), total suspended solids (TSS), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP) and fecal or thermotolerant coliforms (FC) present in treated wastewater by applying several statistical tests. The results showed that the lognormal distribution is really the most representative of the behavior of almost all these constitu- ents, which is in agreement with the ﬁndings from the above- mentioned authors.

Consequently, the COR developed by [Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [(1979),](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) based on the assumed lognormality of the data, can be used to estimate the reliability of the treatment plants, that is, the fraction of time at which the efﬂuent concentration does not exceed some standard value. For that purpose, the CVs calculated for the WWTP studied were used. If, for example, a standard of 60 mg L 1 is to be achieved 90% of the time, the process must be designed or operated to achieve a speciﬁc mean efﬂuent concentration, given the existing variability.

The COR relates the values of the mean design concentra- tions to the standard to be achieved, on a probability basis:

mx ¼ðCORÞXs, (1)

where mx is the mean efﬂuent concentration (design or operational values) (mg L 1), Xs the efﬂuent concentration as speciﬁed by the discharge standard (mg L 1) and COR the coefﬁcient of reliability.

The COR is calculated from the following equation ([Niku](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [et](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [al.,](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese) [1979)](#references-ambiental-abes-rio-de-janeiro-anais-rio-de-janeiro-sn-in-portuguese):

pﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃ qﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃ COR ¼ CV2 þ 1 exp Z1 a lnðCV2 þ 1Þ , (2)

where CV is the coefﬁcient of variation (standard deviation divided by mean); a the probability of failure of meeting the standards and Z1 a the standardized normal variate (obtained from the standard normal variate tables).

From the COR obtained, it was possible to determine the design concentrations that would be required to achieve the discharge standards.

(2). The resulting value of COR is 0.47, which can also be obtained from [Table](#33-cor-values-obtained-in-the-study) [4](#33-cor-values-obtained-in-the-study) for CV ¼ 0.6 and a reliability level of 95%:

pﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃ qﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃﬃ COR ¼ 0:62 þ 1 exp 1:645 lnð0:62 þ 1Þ ¼ 0:47.

This means that, in order to comply with the standards 95% of the time, the mean efﬂuent concentration should be, accord- ing to Eq. (1): mx ¼ COR Xs ¼ 0.47 Xs. For a standard of 60 mg L 1, this means that the design efﬂuent concentration (assumed equal to the mean value) should be mx ¼

0.47 60 ¼ 28 mg L 1. For a lower reliability level of 80% and the same CV of 0.60, from [Table](#33-cor-values-obtained-in-the-study) [4](#33-cor-values-obtained-in-the-study) one obtains COR ¼ 0.73. Therefore, in order to comply with the standards 80% of the time, a mean efﬂuent concentration of 0.73 60 ¼ 44 mg L 1 is required (naturally higher, that is, less stringent than the value required for a 95% reliability level). However, for the reliability level of 95%, if the CV value were higher, say, CV ¼ 1.2, COR would be 0.33, indicating that the mean efﬂuent concentration should be 0.33 60 ¼ 20 mg L 1. Simi- lar calculations can be done for different CV values and reliability levels.

more detailed discussion about the interpretation of COR for the various CVs at different levels of reliability is given in Section 3.6, where some probabilistic concepts that should be introduced both in design and in setting discharge standards are discussed.

### 3.3. COR values obtained in the study

The COR of the components of interest, taking into con- sideration the CV of the WWTP in operation, have been calculated for a level of reliability of 95% (Eq. (2)). The mean values of CV and COR of the six technologies, considering all constituents are presented in [Table](#34-design-and-operation-concentrations-required-to-achieve-the-discharge-standards) [5](#34-design-and-operation-concentrations-required-to-achieve-the-discharge-standards) and in Fig. 2, in the form of box-whisker plots, showing the maximum and minimum values, the 25% and 75% percentiles and the median of the values.

It is seen that, with the exception of coliforms, most of the mean CV values obtained for the other constituents are lower than 1.0. Coliforms, whose values generally vary in orders of magnitude, are the exception, and CV values greater than 1.0 are found.

The plots show the general trend that, for the same level of reliability (95%), a higher value of the CV leads to a lower COR. In general, the lowest COR values were obtained in the AS process, considering the median and the percentages. A considerable percentage of WWTP of this type presented CV above 1.0, a fact explained by the low efﬂuent concentrations, in many cases lower than the standard deviations. It should be noted that low CV values and, consequently, high COR values do not necessarily imply a good performance (since the efﬂuent concentrations of the components have not been taken into consideration), but simply a more stable operating condition.

Low COR values imply the need for lower design efﬂuent concentrations, since these will be obtained by multiplying the COR by the discharge standard value to be achieved.

### 3.4. Design and operation concentrations required to achieve the discharge standards

Table 6 and Fig. 3 show the mean design concentrations, which would lead to the achievement of the discharge standards: BOD ¼ 60 mg L 1;COD¼ 200mgL 1;TSS¼ 60 mg L 1; TN ¼ 20 mg L 1; TP¼ 2mgL 1 and FC ¼ 103 MPN100 mL 1, as well as the actual concentrations observed for each treatment technology. As discussed in Section 2.2, these standards correspond, in some cases, to hypothetical targets based on intermediate standards usually adopted by some Brazilian states and in other developing regions in the world. Design concentrations were calculated by means of Eq. (1) for each system, using their CV and a ¼ 0.05.

Fig. 3 shows the large distance between the design value, necessary to ensure that 95% of the results meet the prevailing discharge standards, and the actual efﬂuent concentration observed for the WWTPs. In general, the simpler treatment systems, represented by ST+AF, FP and AP+FP, showed much higher efﬂuent concentrations in terms of BOD, COD and TSS.

However, all technologies presented a great variability in terms of the mean efﬂuent concentrations of the constituents TN, TP and FC. Some AS and UASB+POST plants achieved very good performance, showing that the actual efﬂuent concen- trations would meet much more restrictive discharge stan- dards than those considered for BOD, COD and TSS.

### 3.5. Expected percentage of compliance with the discharge standards

It was also investigated which percentage of compliance the treatment technologies would achieve, if they kept the same operating conditions, by using Eq. (4). The results obtained, considering the discharge standards adopted, are presented in the form of box-whisker plots in Fig. 4.

It should be noted that the highest compliance percentages were obtained in the AS and UASB+POST technologies and the worst results were obtained by ST+AF, which presented a very small variation among the several WWTPs within this process (only one plant achieved a high percentage of expected compliance with BOD and COD discharge stan- dards). The behavior of ST+AF improved regarding TSS, presenting a higher number of WWTP obtaining some

technologies

Coefﬁcient of reliability (COR)

nitrogen.

percentage of compliance with this standard, but the expected performance was critical, considering the percen- tage obtained by FP and AP+FP. It is worth mentioning that the low expected performance in terms of nutrients was ex- pected, since none of the analyzed technologies has been designed for either nitrogen or phosphorus removal. How- ever, the good performance presented by the AS process, considering TP, is somewhat unexpected, with 25% percentile equal to 74% (which means that 75% of the waste- water treatment plants presented an expected compliance above 74%).

The plots presented in Fig. 5, showing the percentage of compliance with the standards, provide a better visualization of what can be expected for the various treatment technol- ogies. According to the plots showing the expected compli- ance with the 60 mg L 1 BOD standard, taking the ST+AF as an example, 80% of the WWTPs would fail to achieve compliance above 16%. On the other hand, 20% of the WWTPs in the AS and UASB+POST technologies would ensure compliance above 99% and 96%, respectively.

very small. Use of probabilistic methods in setting discharge standards is a realistic and practical approach from an operational point of view. By knowing or assuming the variability of plant performance, it should be possible to determine what average efﬂuent quality must be maintained to meet a standard with some predetermined probability.
